nodes.line: Every camera in this town wants a close-up. I keep the footage that looked away.

options.label: Ask about the unmarked film reel
options.response: It records the same surveillance test in three time zones. Denver can weatherproof it. Chicago can put it on the air.

options.label: Deliver Inez's solar cipher
options.response: These frames are not sun damage. They are instructions written in glare. Mae in Boston will know the checksum.

options.label: Show her the watermarked record
options.response: The watermark resolves under old studio lamps. Mae's page names a camera office that officially opens next year.

options.label: Return the eastbound broadcast ledger
options.response: Coast to mountains to lake and back. That is a national release, whether they approve it or not.

options.label: Ask who owns the backlot
options.response: Four shell companies and one retired pigeon. The pigeon has the cleanest books.

nodes.line: Union Station has more antennas than trains. I service the ones listed as decorative palms.

options.label: Ask about the decorative palms
options.response: They shed no leaves and need a firmware window every Tuesday. Very drought tolerant.

options.label: Ask about eastbound routes
options.response: Everything east goes through weather, freight, or paperwork. Usually all three.

options.label: Step away from the signal cabinet
options.response: Mind the platform cameras. They arrive before the trains do.

nodes.line: Broadcast local, interfere national. That is not a slogan. It is an electrical condition.

options.label: Ask about tonight's show
options.response: Port traffic, coded dedications, and twenty minutes of gulls jamming a patrol frequency.

options.label: Ask where the signal reaches
options.response: On a clear night? Catalina. On a strange night? Cleveland.

options.label: Sign off
options.response: Stay tuned. Staying tuned is different from being tracked. Mostly.

nodes.line: The forecast is public. The list of people who checked it is not.

options.label: Ask about the duplicate pressure maps
options.response: The desert and the coast logged the same impossible storm. I need readings from both before the map corrects itself.

options.label: Deliver Marisol's master reel
options.response: I sealed it against snow, dust, and official curiosity. Lena in Chicago has the freight band to broadcast it.

options.label: Altitude-test Mae's copied seal
options.response: The ink expands above five thousand feet. It reveals a Chicago routing number beneath the colonial date.

options.label: Return the hurricane comparison
options.response: Same pressure signature, two thousand miles apart. The weather is sharing an account.

options.label: Ask about mountain snow
options.response: It melts into five states and reports to six agencies before breakfast.

nodes.line: The trail counters count hikers. The new ones count hesitation.

options.label: Inspect the trail counters
options.response: Step past twice and it calls you indecisive. Step past three times and it calls a ranger.

options.label: Ask about the summit uplink
options.response: Good line of sight from here to every bad idea on the plains.

options.label: Head downhill
options.response: Take water. Altitude makes the forms feel heavier.

nodes.line: Colfax runs long enough to outlast most alibis.

options.label: Ask about the motel ledgers
options.response: Every room is vacant and every key is warm. Tourism is recovering strangely.

options.label: Read the mile marker
options.response: It says Boston one way, Los Angeles the other, and COMPLY straight ahead.

options.label: Continue down the avenue
options.response: Keep moving. Parked cars get entered into the census.

nodes.line: Sunlight is free. They are trying to make the frequencies subscription only.

options.label: Ask about the solar cipher
options.response: The array burned a message into its own cells. Los Angeles can read the frames. Boston can prove they are old.

options.label: Deliver Eli's pressure ledger
options.response: The desert reading matches a storm surge. Sol in Miami keeps the coastal half of this impossible weather.

options.label: Dry and restore Sol's tide ledger
options.response: Salt hid a rail coordinate in the margins. Lena in Chicago can match it to inland freight.

options.label: Return the archival checksum
options.response: The signal crossed both coasts and came home older than when it left. That is proof enough for me.

options.label: Browse the repair shelves
options.response: Everything works. Nothing broadcasts under its legal name.

nodes.line: Freight comes through at night with no logos and too many cooling fans.

options.label: Ask about the unmarked freight
options.response: It heads west empty and returns heavy. The seals say municipal weather.

options.label: Trace the yard power
options.response: Half the draw goes uphill to an array that claims to be a picnic shelter.

options.label: Clear the tracks
options.response: Good. The next train is not on a schedule you are cleared to read.

nodes.line: Balloons drift. Surveillance platforms maintain an approved scenic altitude.

options.label: Ask which balloons are real
options.response: The real ones wave back. The others rotate exactly twelve degrees per minute.

options.label: Ask about the mountain shadow
options.response: Radio goes quiet there. People remember their own thoughts for a few minutes.

options.label: Release the tether
options.response: Let it rise. The sky has less paperwork than the ground.

nodes.line: Chicago moves the country's freight. The country moves its mistakes through Chicago.

options.label: Ask about the train with no arrival
options.response: Its seal appears in Boston records two centuries early. Mae has the archive. Denver can test the ink.

options.label: Broadcast Marisol's weatherproof reel
options.response: The freight band carried it east in eleven seconds. Here is the ledger before the network denies hearing it.

options.label: Match Inez's restored coordinates
options.response: They belong to a container that left Miami wet and reached Chicago before it departed.

options.label: Return the verified seal
options.response: Now the ghost has a routing number. That makes it somebody's budget problem.

options.label: Ask how far down the road goes
options.response: Far enough that daylight becomes an administrative rumor.

nodes.line: The river changed direction once. The cameras still file reports facing the old way.

options.label: Ask which bridge listens
options.response: The one that opens when no boat is coming. It needs the clear view.

options.label: Ask about the lake relays
options.response: Fresh water, saltwater paperwork. Signals wash ashore from every coast.

options.label: Let the bridge close
options.response: Stand clear. Infrastructure gets territorial after dark.

nodes.line: The stockyards closed. The time clocks stayed employed.

options.label: Inspect the time clocks
options.response: They punch in workers who retired before the cameras were installed.

options.label: Ask what the union tracks
options.response: Wages, injuries, and which break-room vents started asking questions.

options.label: Clock out
options.response: Keep the stub. It proves you were here and also that you were not scheduled.

nodes.line: Boston keeps every record, especially the ones written before the event.

options.label: Ask about the page dated next winter
options.response: The watermark is modern, the paper is colonial, and the signature belongs to an office in Miami. Start there.

options.label: Show her Chicago's freight seal
options.response: It appears on a harbor manifest from 1791. Take this copy to Denver; altitude separates old ink from new lies.

options.label: Verify Marisol's decoded frame
options.response: The checksum predates the solar panel by eighty years. Inez deserves the impossible original.

options.label: Return the film scan
options.response: Excellent. The archive now contains proof, a duplicate, and a denial in triplicate.

options.label: Ask how deep the archive goes
options.response: Three floors below sea level and one floor below municipal memory.

name: Priya Shah
role: Transit Counsel, Lost Green Line Stop

nodes.line: The train is delayed by an inquiry into whether this platform legally exists.

options.label: Ask where the stop appears on maps
options.response: Only on maps printed during leap years and one restaurant placemat.

options.label: Ask about the legal inquiry
options.response: The city sued the platform. The platform failed to appear. Default judgment is pending.

options.label: Take the stairs
options.response: A practical choice. I cannot advise it officially.

nodes.line: The board reviews ethics upstairs. I review what they throw away downstairs.

options.label: Ask about discarded minutes
options.response: Every concern was noted. None survived the recycling schedule.

options.label: Ask about the sealed lab
options.response: They study public trust. The specimens keep trying to escape.

options.label: Exit through peer review
options.response: Two reviewers objected, so naturally you are approved.

nodes.line: Every container has a declared origin. The tide keeps submitting corrections.

options.label: Ask about the waterlogged ledger
options.response: It lists inland ports at sea level and Miami cargo in Chicago yesterday. Inez can restore the salt damage.

options.label: Deliver Inez's desert calibration
options.response: It matches our hurricane sensor exactly. Take this comparison back to Eli before the next forecast changes history.

options.label: Inspect Mae's watermarked page
options.response: Ultraviolet light reveals a Los Angeles film code. Marisol Vega will know which studio printed it.

options.label: Return the inland shipping match
options.response: So the tide reaches Chicago now. Good. I was worried geography still meant something.

options.label: Ask who watches the causeway
options.response: Customs watches cargo. Flock watches customs. The gulls watch everybody.

nodes.line: The cafecito is strong, the signal is stronger, and neither has a permit.

options.label: Ask about the neighborhood station
options.response: Music by day, storm routes by night, names of missing cameras whenever needed.

options.label: Ask what is in the coffee
options.response: Sugar, courage, and enough voltage to cross Biscayne Bay.

options.label: Leave a dedication
options.response: I will play it after the weather alert and before the official correction.

nodes.line: The sawgrass does not need cameras. It remembers where you stepped.

options.label: Ask about the wetland sensors
options.response: Half measure water. Half measure people looking at the water.

options.label: Ask for the dry path
options.response: There is no dry path. There is only the path where the paperwork floats.

options.label: Back away from the waterline
options.response: Slowly. The alligators are not agents, but they do accept tips.
